subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which prominent opposition leader founded the Congress Socialist Party within the Congress in 1934 and later led the Socialist Party?
questions.explanation: Acharya Narendra Deva was a pioneering democratic socialist thinker who served as the founding president of the Congress Socialist Party (CSP) in 1934.

questions.question: Which princely state was the first part of India to hold an election based on Universal Adult Franchise in June 1948?
questions.explanation: The Maharaja of Manipur, Bodhachandra Singh, conducted legislative elections based on universal adult franchise in June 1948, making Manipur a constitutional monarchy.

questions.question: Which committee consisting of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya was constituted in 1948 to examine the linguistic reorganization of states?
questions.explanation: The JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) examined the Dhar Commission's report and advised postponing linguistic reorganisation.

questions.question: Which young economist drafted the First Five Year Plan and advocated that India should 'hasten slowly' for the first two decades?
questions.explanation: K.N. Raj, a young economist involved in drafting the First Five Year Plan, warned against premature rapid industrialisation and advised gradual agrarian capital accumulation.

questions.question: Which massive multipurpose river valley project was undertaken during the First Five Year Plan to boost irrigation and hydroelectric power in northern India?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Nangal Dam on the Sutlej river was a flagship infrastructure undertaking of the First Five Year Plan, celebrated by Nehru as a 'temple of modern India'.

questions.question: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India who also retained the portfolio of External Affairs throughout his tenure?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru exercised decisive personal leadership over India's foreign policy as Prime Minister and Minister for External Affairs from 1947 to 1964.

questions.question: Which international crisis in 1956 witnessed India vigorously condemning the British-French-Israeli military aggression, in contrast to its muted response to the Soviet intervention in Hungary?
questions.explanation: India strongly protested the neo-colonial military invasion of Egypt during the Suez Crisis of 1956, while maintaining a restrained diplomatic stance regarding the Soviet intervention in Hungary.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth General Election of 1967, which regional party secured a clear legislative majority in Madras state (Tamil Nadu), ending Congress rule?
questions.explanation: The DMK, led by C.N. Annadurai, secured a landslide victory in Madras (Tamil Nadu) in 1967, becoming the first non-Congress party to secure a single-party majority in any Indian state.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following the formal split of the Indian National Congress in November 1969, the faction led by Indira Gandhi came to be known as:
questions.explanation: In the 1969 split, Indira Gandhi's group was termed Congress (Requisitionists) or Congress (R), while the Syndicate-led conservative wing was known as Congress (Organisation) or Congress (O).

questions.question: In which city did Jayaprakash Narayan address a massive historic rally at the Ramlila Ground on 25 June 1975, announcing a nationwide satyagraha for Indira Gandhi's resignation?
questions.explanation: JP addressed an enormous public rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on 25 June 1975, urging government employees and armed forces not to obey unconstitutional orders.

questions.question: Which leading English daily newspapers in India protested government pre-censorship during the Emergency by leaving their editorial columns blank?
options: A) The Times of India and The Hindu
B) Hindustan Times and The Pioneer
C) The Indian Express and The Statesman
D) The Tribune and National Herald
questions.explanation: Newspapers like The Indian Express and The Statesman registered protest against press censorship by publishing blank editorial spaces.

questions.question: How many Lok Sabha seats were won by the Janata Party and its allies in the historic sixth General Election of March 1977?
options: D) 330 seats (Janata Party won 295 on its own)
questions.explanation: The Janata Party and its electoral allies secured 330 out of 542 Lok Sabha seats in March 1977, with the Janata Party winning 295 seats on its own, defeating the Congress.

questions.question: In which year was the historic Assam Accord signed between the Central Government under Rajiv Gandhi and the leaders of the AASU and AAGSP?
questions.explanation: The Assam Accord was signed on 15 August 1985, setting 24 March 1971 as the cut-off date to identify and deport illegal foreigners.

questions.question: Which Naga leader formed the Naga National Council (NNC) and declared the independence of Nagaland in 1951?
questions.explanation: Angami Zapu Phizo led the Naga National Council (NNC) which launched an armed campaign for an independent sovereign Naga homeland.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairman of the Second Backward Classes Commission by the Janata Party government in January 1979?
questions.explanation: Bindeshwari Prasad Mandal (B.P. Mandal), a former Chief Minister of Bihar, was appointed Chairman of the Second Backward Classes Commission in 1979.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which treaty signed in 1955 served as the collective military defense pact of the Soviet Union and its Eastern European communist allies?
questions.explanation: The Warsaw Treaty Organisation (Warsaw Pact) was created by the Soviet Union in 1955 to counter the Western alliance, NATO.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In which month and year was the Soviet Union officially dissolved, marking the end of the Cold War bipolar world order?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union ceased to exist in December 1991 following declarations by Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus and the subsequent resignation of Mikhail Gorbachev on 25 December 1991.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which US economic aid plan announced in 1947 provided financial assistance to revive the war-ravaged economies of Western Europe?
questions.explanation: The Marshall Plan, initiated by US Secretary of State George Marshall, channeled billions of dollars to rebuild Western Europe and establish the OEEC in 1948.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: In which year did the People's Republic of China become a formal member of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
questions.explanation: China officially joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) in December 2001, integrating its economy deeply into global trade networks.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which country was admitted as the eighth member state of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) in 2007?
questions.explanation: Afghanistan joined SAARC as its eighth member at the 14th SAARC Summit held in New Delhi in April 2007.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: The Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) was deployed to Sri Lanka in 1987 under which bilateral peace accord?
options: A) Indo-Sri Lanka Accord signed by Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene
B) Colombo Declaration signed by Indira Gandhi and Sirimavo Bandaranaike
C) Kandy Accord signed by Lal Bahadur Shastri and Dudley Senanayake
D) Galle Agreement signed by P.V. Narasimha Rao and Chandrika Kumaratunga
questions.explanation: The Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord was signed on 29 July 1987 by Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and Sri Lankan President J.R. Jayewardene, leading to IPKF deployment.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which international trade organisation was established on 1 January 1995 as the direct institutional successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)?
options: A) United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)
questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO) commenced operations on 1 January 1995 following the Marrakesh Agreement, replacing GATT.

questions.question: Which concept of security expands the focus beyond military protection of the state to safeguarding the lives and dignity of individual human beings?
questions.explanation: Human Security focuses on the protection of people from threats to their survival, livelihood, and dignity ('freedom from fear' and 'freedom from want').

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which book published in 1972 by an international think-tank known as the Club of Rome dramatically dramatized the depletion of the Earth's natural resources?
questions.explanation: The Club of Rome published 'The Limits to Growth' in 1972, highlighting ecological perils and depletion of natural resources due to unchecked industrial expansion.

questions.question: In which American city did violent protests and massive civil society demonstrations paralyze the WTO Ministerial Conference in November 1999?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Seattle WTO protests brought together environmentalists, labour unions, and consumer activists, marking a turning point in global resistance to neo-liberal globalisation.

questions.question: Which socialist leader broke away from the Praja Socialist Party to form the Samyukta Socialist Party (SSP) and championed reservations for backward classes?
questions.explanation: Ram Manohar Lohia parted ways with the PSP to establish the Socialist Party and later SSP, arguing vigorously for preferential quotas for backward castes, Dalits, and women.

questions.question: How did the Government of India determine the accession of the princely state of Junagadh after its Nawab initially acceded to Pakistan in 1947?
options: A) Through an immediate military annexation code-named Operation Vijay
B) Through arbitration by the International Court of Justice at The Hague
C) Through a public plebiscite held in February 1948 where citizens voted overwhelmingly to join India
D) Through an agreement signed by the Governor-General Lord Mountbatten
questions.explanation: Following the Nawab's flight to Karachi, a plebiscite was conducted in Junagadh in February 1948, in which over 99% of the electorate voted to join the Indian Union.

questions.question: During the intense policy debates over the First and Second Five Year Plans, which politician resigned from the Congress and later formed the Bharatiya Lok Dal to champion the cause of agriculture over heavy industry?
questions.explanation: Choudhary Charan Singh forcefully articulated that planning was unfairly prioritizing heavy industry at the expense of agriculture and rural peasantry.

questions.question: Which international border line demarcating India and China in the eastern sector (Arunachal Pradesh) was repudiated by Beijing as a legacy of British imperialism?
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line was drawn during the 1914 Simla Convention between Britain and Tibet, which China refused to recognize, claiming sovereignty over the territory.

questions.question: During the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War, Pakistani forces in East Pakistan surrendered unconditionally under which commanding general on 16 December 1971?
options: D) Major General Rao Farman Ali
questions.explanation: Pakistani commander Lt. Gen. A.A.K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender in Dhaka before Lt. Gen. J.S. Aurora of the Indian Eastern Command, surrendering 93,000 soldiers.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: What radical socio-economic program did Indira Gandhi present to the Congress Working Committee in May 1967 to steer the party towards a left-of-centre socialist agenda?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi formulated the Ten-Point Programme in May 1967, which included social control of banks, nationalisation of general insurance, ceiling on urban property, and abolition of princely privileges.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the 1971 Lok Sabha elections, an alliance of major non-Congress opposition parties including Congress(O), SSP, PSP, Jana Sangh, and Swatantra Party was forged under the name:
questions.explanation: The non-communist opposition parties formed the 'Grand Alliance' in 1971 with the singular platform of 'Indira Hatao', but suffered an overwhelming electoral defeat.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act passed by the Janata Party government in 1978 dismantled the authoritarian provisions introduced by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) restored constitutional safeguards, replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352, and made the right to life non-suspendable.

questions.question: Which constitutional provision granting special autonomous status to the state of Jammu and Kashmir was effectively nullified by Parliament in August 2019?
questions.explanation: Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, which granted special autonomous privileges to Jammu and Kashmir, was abrogated in August 2019, bifurcating the state into two Union Territories.

questions.question: Which political front formed the Union government in 1996 with outside support from the Congress, headed first by H.D. Deve Gowda and then by I.K. Gujral?
questions.explanation: The United Front coalition formed the government in 1996 with external support from the Congress Party, led by H.D. Deve Gowda and subsequently by I.K. Gujral until 1998.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the Baltic republics that declared their independence from the Soviet Union in 1991?
questions.explanation: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania constitute the three Baltic republics that declared independence; Belarus is an East Slavic republic that joined the CIS in 1991.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which phrase describes the unique diplomatic style of ASEAN characterized by informal, non-confrontational, and consensus-based decision-making?
questions.explanation: The 'ASEAN Way' is the celebrated form of interaction among Southeast Asian nations that emphasizes informality, mutual respect, non-intervention, and quiet consensus.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which multilateral grouping comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China, and later South Africa was formed as an emerging alternative geopolitical bloc?
questions.explanation: BRICS was formed by emerging economic powers (Brazil, Russia, India, China, with South Africa joining in 2010) to challenge Western hegemony in global governance.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In the Maldives, which pro-democracy leader was elected President in 2008 following the transition to a competitive multi-party system?
questions.explanation: Mohamed Nasheed of the Maldivian Democratic Party (MDP) won the first multi-party democratic presidential election in 2008, ending the 30-year rule of Gayoom.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which UN Secretary-General proposed a set of comprehensive criteria in 1997 for selecting new permanent members to the UN Security Council?
questions.explanation: In 1997, UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan initiated an inquiry suggesting criteria including economic strength, population size, defense contributions, and democratic credentials.

questions.question: What is the key distinction in international law between 'Refugees' and 'Internally Displaced Persons' (IDPs)?
options: A) Refugees have crossed an international border fleeing persecution, whereas IDPs remain within their country's borders
B) Refugees leave voluntarily for economic gains, while IDPs are forcibly evacuated by military forces
C) Refugees are protected exclusively by the World Bank, while IDPs are handled by NATO
D) Refugees possess diplomatic immunity, whereas IDPs are stripped of citizenship rights
questions.explanation: Refugees cross international boundaries to escape persecution, violence, or war, whereas IDPs are displaced within the national borders of their own homeland.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In which year did the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) get adopted?
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted on 11 December 1997 in Kyoto, Japan, setting legally binding greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for industrialized nations.

questions.question: Which of the following was a key structural characteristic of the First Lok Sabha election in 1952 regarding parliamentary constituencies?
options: A) Every constituency was strictly single-member with simple plurality system
B) Elections were conducted under a nationwide proportional representation party-list system
C) Over 80 constituencies were multi-member constituencies electing two or three representatives to provide representation to SCs and STs
D) Only literate taxpayers above the age of 25 possessed the constitutional right to vote
questions.explanation: In the 1952 and 1957 elections, India utilized two-member (and one three-member) constituencies to ensure representation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, abolished in 1961.

questions.question: Which three key principles were identified by Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon as the bedrock of the Government of India's approach toward princely states?
options: A) Complete abolition of royal titles, immediate nationalisation of all royal properties, and deportation of uncooperative rulers
B) Imposition of Hindi as the sole state language, abolition of princely treasuries, and mandatory accession to Pakistan
C) Appointment of military governors, suspension of civil courts, and dissolution of all local municipal bodies
D) The people of princely states clearly wished to be part of the Union, the government was flexible in granting autonomy, and the consolidation of territorial boundaries was supreme
questions.explanation: The three considerations guided Patel: the popular desire to join India, government flexibility in autonomy negotiations, and the non-negotiable imperative of national unity and integrity.

questions.question: What was the administrative 'zoning policy' enforced by the central and state governments during the severe Bihar food crisis of 1965-1967?
options: A) Trade restrictions that prohibited private traders from transporting foodgrains across state boundaries
B) The mandatory allocation of all agricultural land exclusively for sugarcane production
C) The complete confiscation of private granaries without monetary compensation
D) The compulsory eviction of tenant cultivators from drought-affected rural districts
questions.explanation: Under the government's food zoning policy, movement of foodgrains across state borders was banned, preventing surplus grain from other states from reaching famine-stricken Bihar.

questions.question: What was the formal diplomatic status of the Dalai Lama's headquarters established in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh, following his exile in 1959?
options: A) India formally recognized Tibet as an independent sovereign republic with full diplomatic embassy status in New Delhi
B) India granted religious asylum and humanitarian shelter but strictly prohibited any anti-China political activity from Indian soil
C) India signed a mutual defense pact with the Tibetan government-in-exile pledging military liberation of Lhasa
D) India placed the Dalai Lama under preventive administrative custody under the Defense of India Rules
questions.explanation: India extended generous humanitarian and spiritual sanctuary to the Dalai Lama and thousands of Tibetan refugees while officially maintaining that political activity against Beijing was barred.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution, invoked during the Emergency, barred courts from entertaining applications challenging the detention of individuals under MISA (Maintenance of Internal Security Act)?
options: A) Article 368 clause (4) removing judicial review over constitutional amendments
B) Article 356 dismissing the democratically elected state ministries
C) Presidential Order under Article 359 suspending the enforcement of Article 21 and Article 14
D) Article 365 directing state executives to obey central administrative directives
questions.explanation: Under Article 359, President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued an order suspending citizens' right to move any court for enforcement of Articles 14, 21, and 22, immunizing MISA detentions.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In the Caucasus region of the Russian Federation, which Muslim-majority republic witnessed a protracted, brutal secessionist conflict in which Russian forces used heavy aerial bombardments?
questions.explanation: Chechnya declared independence in 1991, leading to two devastating wars with Moscow (1994-1996 and 1999-2009) with extensive destruction and heavy civilian casualties.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Under which historic agreement signed in 1985 in a Luxembourg town did several European nations agree to abolish border checks and facilitate free movement of individuals?
questions.explanation: The Schengen Agreement was signed in 1985 in Schengen, Luxembourg, leading to the creation of Europe's border-free Schengen Area with common visa policies.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What key distinction was established in the Kyoto Protocol between Annex I countries and non-Annex I developing countries like India and China?
options: A) Developing nations were forced to pay carbon tariffs to industrialized nations to subsidize green energy
B) Annex I countries were prohibited from trading carbon emission credits on international markets
C) Developing nations were barred from utilizing fossil fuels for industrial power generation
D) Annex I industrialized nations were subject to mandatory binding emission cuts, whereas developing nations were exempt from binding reduction targets
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol exempted non-Annex I developing nations (including India and China) from binding emissions reductions because their per capita emissions were historic fractions of the developed world.
